albums.blurb: Dexter Gordon was the towering tenor saxophonist of the bebop generation, and Go! is the peak of his early-sixties Blue Note comeback, cut in a single August 1962 session with pianist Sonny Clark, bassist Butch Warren and drummer Billy Higgins. It was recorded just before Gordon left for Europe, where he would stay for most of the next fourteen years, and its mix of long-striding originals like "Cheese Cake" with ballads and standards is entirely instrumental quartet playing.
albums.reception: In 2019 the Library of Congress selected Go! for preservation in the National Recording Registry as "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant."

albums.blurb: Steve Lacy came up as the teenage guitarist and producer of The Internet, working from an iPhone, before producing for Kendrick Lamar and Solange. Gemini Rights is his second solo album, a breakup record that trades the lo-fi sketches of Apollo XXI (2019) for tightly written guitar-led R&B and bossa-tinged funk-pop across a compact ten tracks.
albums.reception: Gemini Rights won Best Progressive R&B Album at the 2023 Grammy Awards, debuted at number 7 on the Billboard 200, and its single "Bad Habit" became Lacy's first number-one on the Hot 100.

albums.blurb: Prefab Sprout formed around County Durham songwriter Paddy McAloon, whose wordy, harmonically rich writing made him a critics' favourite among British songwriters of the eighties. Steve McQueen, the band's second album, was produced by Thomas Dolby, who streamlined McAloon's songs into sleek, jazz-inflected pop; in the United States it was retitled Two Wheels Good after objections from the actor's estate.
albums.reception: NME named Steve McQueen the fourth-best album of 1985, and it reached number 21 on the UK Albums Chart.
